description: Fig. 4 is a composite EBSD figure combining four band-contrast maps with their Schmid-factor histograms, an orientation colour key and a 3-D trend plot. Panels (a)-(d) are band-contrast maps of Fe-8Mn-6Al-0.2C low-density steel deformed to true strains of 0.03, 0.10, 0.20 and 0.27; each has a 5 μm scale bar, a grey ferrite matrix with outlined grain boundaries, and individual retained-austenite grains shaded in rainbow colours by Schmid factor (red = high, blue = low). Each map contains a red inset histogram of Number Fraction versus Schmid factor (x = 0.25-0.50) labelled 0.03, 0.1, 0.2 and 0.27 respectively; several are also supplied magnified, with y = Number Fraction reaching 0.20-0.30. A separate "Face Centered Cubic" inverse-pole-figure colour key (corners 001, 101, 111) is included. Panel (e) is a 3-D ribbon/waterfall plot with axes Schmid factor (0.30-0.50), strain (0.05-0.25) and Number Fraction (0.000-0.208 on the right axis), holding four curves labelled ε=0.03 (dark blue), ε=0.10 (red), ε=0.20 (magenta) and ε=0.27 (black). The figure demonstrates that the retained-austenite Schmid-factor population migrates to lower values with increasing strain, i.e. low-Schmid-factor austenite remains untransformed.

observations.observation: Panels (a)-(d) are band-contrast EBSD maps with 5 μm scale bars showing a grey matrix with outlined grain boundaries and individually coloured retained-austenite grains.
Each of panels (a)-(d) carries a red inset histogram of Number Fraction versus Schmid factor (x range 0.25-0.50) labelled with the strain value 0.03, 0.1, 0.2 and 0.27 respectively.
The caption states the figure combines band contrast maps and Schmid factor maps at true strains (a) 0.03, (b) 0.10, (c) 0.20 and (d) 0.27, with (e) showing the changed trend of Schmid factor.
The standalone magnified histogram labelled 0.03 shows a single broad population whose maximum lies in the 0.45-0.47 Schmid-factor bins, at a Number Fraction just below 0.20.
The standalone magnified histogram labelled 0.1 has its maximum in the ~0.41 bin, with the tallest bar at about 0.26 Number Fraction.
The magnified histogram labelled 0.2 is bimodal, with the dominant maximum at Schmid factor ~0.35-0.36 and a secondary peak at ~0.42-0.43.
The histogram labelled 0.27 is markedly flatter and noisier than the others, with peaks near 0.34-0.35 and 0.48-0.50 and no single dominant mode.

Panel (e) plots Number Fraction (right axis, 0.000-0.208) against Schmid factor (0.30-0.50) as four marker-lined curves separated along a strain axis (0.05-0.25), labelled ε=0.03 (dark blue), ε=0.10 (red), ε=0.20 (magenta) and ε=0.27 (black).

In panel (e) the ε=0.03 curve peaks near Schmid factor 0.46-0.47, the ε=0.10 curve near 0.41 and the ε=0.20 curve near 0.36, i.e. the population maximum shifts to progressively lower Schmid factor as strain increases.
A 'Face Centered Cubic' inverse-pole-figure colour key triangle with corner labels 001, 101 and 111 is provided, consistent with a rainbow orientation colouring scheme.
The citing text states that grains with a high Schmid factor are indicated in red and those with a very low Schmid factor in blue using rainbow coloring.
The citing text states that at the true strain of 0.03 the relative volume fraction of retained austenite with Schmid factors of 0.45-0.48 was more than 70%.
The citing text states that when the true strain increased to 0.10 the majority of retained austenite had Schmid factors of 0.39-0.42 and the average factor decreased apparently.

The citing text states that at a true strain of 0.20 over 60% of retained austenite had Schmid factors smaller than 0.40, while at a true strain of 0.27 the volume fraction with Schmid factors less than 0.34 decreased to 5%.
The citing text concludes that retained austenite possessing relatively small Schmid factors tends to remain untransformed during tensile deformation.
